macro_blurb: Geopolitical risk is front and center as the US military announced a new wave of strikes on Iran, with Trump signaling Tehran wants to meet even as analysts flag "forever war" risks — a backdrop reinforced by Kalshi traders pricing gasoline above $4 by end-July and United flagging $6 billion in added fuel costs, pressuring the airline complex on both sides of the Atlantic. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Senate Banking testimony on the economy and interest rates is the key macro event, while a separate Fed report noted the World Cup lifted bars and restaurants even as consumers show warning signs. In tech, SpaceX shares slipped below their IPO price post-listing, and Trump publicly attacked New York's AI data center moratorium, keeping the AI infrastructure policy debate live.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a Value-and-Yield exercise, not a growth one. Average Value percentile across the top ten is 88.6 and average Yield is 90.4, against a Quality average of just 52.6 — the machine is paying up for cheapness and cash distribution and explicitly not for balance-sheet quality. Ten of ten picks are US-listed; no European name cleared the bar despite 969 tickers screened. Sector distribution is unusually flat — Utilities, Consumer Defensive and Industrials each contribute two names, with Technology represented by a single deep-value outlier. Composite range is tight (76.2–86.8), so there is no runaway leader, just a cluster of similar setups.

The connecting thread runs through the income trade: HPQ (4.87% yield, 8.8x P/E), KHC (6.38%, P/B 0.72), MO (6.04%, 14.7x) and ES/EIX (4.22% and 4.58%, both top-7% Value in Utilities) all screen in the 92nd-plus Yield percentile with sub-sector-median multiples. Against Warsh's rate testimony this week, that is a coherent duration-sensitive bet on the front-end topping out. BBY, SNA and MAS form a second cluster — cyclicals riding momentum (32%, 10%, 22.5% three-month returns) into earnings while still cheap on FCF yield.

The outlier is CNC: a 71% three-month return, 100th-percentile Value, but ROE of -26% and Elevance-style Medicaid margin pressure in the tape — this is the pick most at odds with the Quality-agnostic screen's blind spot. The conspicuous absence is Financial Services, Energy, Real Estate and Communication Services — four entire sectors blanked, with Energy particularly striking given Iran strikes and Kalshi pricing gasoline above $4. Two things could flip this book inside two weeks: Warsh's testimony repricing the long end (hits every Yield name simultaneously), and any Iran escalation that forces Energy back into leadership and drains the defensive bid.
